rows.subtopic: Deciding what to do with pocket money
rows.subtype: Approach: lending to a friend without a plan [Pitfall]
rows.description: A boy lends his savings to a friend who promises to repay soon but forgets, and he learns to lend only small amounts and agree on a date beforehand.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: adaptive replanning, copying without fit, externalising on paper, impulsive action

rows.subtype: Approach: task decomposition into a packing and route list [Action]
rows.description: A girl helps plan a visit to her grandparents by listing tasks: book tickets, pack clothes, arrange food for the train, and tick them off with her mother the week before.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: buffer and slack, checklist, forward planning, magical thinking, resource and budget planning

rows.subtype: Approach: comparing travel options by cost and comfort [Thinking]
rows.description: A boy compares train, bus and car for a trip to Agra, noting the train is cheaper and safer at night while the car allows stops, and helps the family choose the train.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: buffer and slack, checklist, forward planning, magical thinking, resource and budget planning, task decomposition

rows.subtype: Approach: making a wish list without limits [Pitfall]
rows.description: The child suggests visiting six places in two days, and only when his father points at the map and clock does he see that travel time makes the plan impossible.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: buffer and slack, checklist, forward planning, resource and budget planning, task decomposition

rows.subtype: Approach: adjusting the plan to fit the budget [Revision]
rows.description: After learning the family can spend only ten thousand rupees, the girl removes the water park and keeps the fort and museum, which cost less and everyone still enjoys.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: buffer and slack, checklist, forward planning, magical thinking, task decomposition

rows.subtype: Approach: asking each family member for one wish [Action]
rows.description: To be fair, the boy asks grandma, mother, father and sister to pick one place each, and the family builds the days around these so nobody feels ignored.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: buffer and slack, checklist, forward planning, resource and budget planning, task decomposition

rows.subtype: Approach: preparing for rain and delays [Thinking]
rows.description: A girl thinks the train may be late and it may rain, so she suggests carrying snacks, a plastic sheet and an indoor plan such as a museum for a wet afternoon.

rows.subtype: Approach: leaving the whole plan to the adults [Pitfall]
rows.description: A child shows no interest and does not help, then is upset on the trip because the places do not match what he likes, missing the chance to give his input.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: buffer and slack, checklist, forward planning, magical thinking, resource and budget planning, task decomposition

rows.subtype: Approach: drawing a map with a timetable [Action]
rows.description: The girl sketches the route on paper with boxes for morning, afternoon and evening, and uses it to check that the timings between stops are realistic.

rows.subtype: Approach: packing checklist based on past trips [Thinking]
rows.description: Remembering that last year they forgot medicine and a charger, the boy writes those first on the list, using earlier mistakes to prevent repeats.
